text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.

- Social democrats and conservatives in parliament debate say the government's ongoing privatisation process is positive; centre party MPs criticise the use of proceeds, while the Leftist Alliance rejects the entire process.
- Children from academic or Swedish-speaking families in Finland are more likely than others to study at univirsities, a study by Statistics Finland and the Helsinki education bureau shows.

- Control of listed Finnish companies shifts slowly and the same leaders are on many boards, for example insurer Sampo's CEO Jouko Leskinen who sits on ten different boards and Pohjola's CEO Iiro Viinanen who is on nine.
- Income taxes should be eased and other taxes tightened, for example the tax on electricity for industrial use, says Tuire Santamaki-Vuori, director of the Labour Economic Research Institute.
- The Association of Foreign Trade is restructuring its organisation for better service, says managing director Seppo Harkonen.

- The political battle between Social democrats and the conservatives will tighten, expecially in the budget debate, as the general elections in 1999 draw nearer, says Erkki Tuomioja, chairman of Social Democratic Party's parliamentary group.

- Parliament to have power over municipalities according to a draft proposal for a new law governing mergers of local authorities, says Pekka Myllyniemi, chairman of the committee preparing the change.

- Mutual Suomi's represenatives meeting to decide today on insurer Pohjola's restructuring plans; no consensus has been reached and the decision may even turn into a political battle against Pohjola CEO Iiro Viinanen.
- Municipalities are not preprared for transition to EMU, says professor Paavo Okko at the University of Turku.

- Finnish-speakers seem to support the Swedish language in Finland, says Henrik Lax, chairman of the Swedish-speaking population's national assembly Folktinget, adding he is prepared to discuss abolishing Swedish as an obligatory language in Finnish schools.
